question: Use of regenerative cells in the process of budding is present in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydra** is a **genus** of small, freshwater organisms of the phylum **Cnidaria** and class **Hydrozoa**.
 
• Hydra reproduces asexually through a process known as **budding**.
 
• In budding, a small bud develops on the body of the parent organism, grows by acquiring cells from the parent, and eventually detaches to form a new, genetically identical individual.
 
• This process involves the use of **regenerative cells**, which allow Hydra to regenerate and form new buds.
 
• Hydra's remarkable ability to regenerate is due to the presence of **stem cells** that can differentiate into any cell type needed for growth and repair.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Planaria**__

 __
 
• **Planaria** are flatworms known for their ability to regenerate lost body parts, but they reproduce primarily through **fission** rather than budding.
 
• They belong to the class **Turbellaria** in the phylum **Platyhelminthes**.
 
 
 
• **Amoeba**__
 __
 
• An **Amoeba** is a single-celled organism that primarily reproduces through a process called **binary fission**, not budding.
 
• It belongs to the phylum **Amoebozoa**.
 
 
 
• **Spirogyra**__
 
 
• **Spirogyra** is a filamentous green alga that reproduces through **fragmentation** and **sexual reproduction**, not budding.
 
• It belongs to the class **Zygnematophyceae** in the phylum **Chlorophyta**.
